lines.text: Do you know each of the Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables is made of twenty-seven thousand, five hundred and seventy-two steel wires?
Its towers rise two hundred and twenty-seven metres above the water. And twelve hundred and eighty metres of road hang between them.
Because the road doesn't rest on the towers. It hangs.
A truck pushes down on the deck. The deck hangs from vertical steel ropes. And the ropes hang from the two main cables.
The cables run over the tops of the towers. And the towers only push straight down, into the sea floor.
At each end, the cables dive into concrete anchorages. Each one weighs sixty thousand tons.
Now look inside one cable. It's ninety-two centimetres thick.
And those are made of twenty-seven thousand, five hundred and seventy-two wires, each about five millimetres thick.
They were spun across the strait, one wire at a time, then squeezed together into a perfect circle.
And the whole road moves. Heat stretches the cables, and the middle of the deck sinks. Cold shortens them, and it rises.
It was built to move more than three metres down, and almost two metres up.
Its colour began as a primer. The architect kept it, partly because it stands out in the fog.
Thousands of wires, bundled into one cable. Orbi Transfer does the same with your folders.
Drop in a whole folder, hundreds of files, and it travels as one bundle, up to twenty gigabytes.
On the other side, it unpacks back into a folder. No app, no login.
